thread:
sasha: Quick follow-up from yesterday's incident report — link to postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-kv-eviction-latency. We identified a recurring pattern: median seq len spikes >150 causing prefix/KV eviction thrash. Need to convert remediation items into concrete tests/evals (regression suite, new promptset, load test, and a quarterly chaos drill). Who volunteers to own each?

jamie: I can own the regression suite and the prompt-set curation. Plan: add a focused vector of inputs that exercises long-context paths + synthetic heavy-short requests. Target PR by end of next sprint (2026-04-02). :thumbsup:

priya: I'll take the load test and perf pipeline integration. Will add a k6 job that ramps to 3x normal token throughput and measures tail latency and kv-miss rate. Will schedule nightly raw runs and weekly stable-run cron. Estimated work: 2 days.

kyle: I'll own the chaos drill and runbook updates. Propose a staged chaos that simulates KV eviction under high seq-length distribution, then run the failover policy to validate fallback models. Also update the emergency rollback playbook.

ops-bot: Incident pattern summary: 2026-03-22T18:14Z - recurring latency spikes correlated with sequences >150; 17% increase in eviction events over baseline; affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Linked analytics: https://observability.redwood/incident/EVCT-3421

sasha: Nice, thanks. Let's capture owners + deliverables here so we can triage into sprint board. Owners and deliverables so far: Jamie -> regression suite + new promptset (PR + eval harness); Priya -> k6 load job + nightly + weekly cron; Kyle -> chaos drill plan + runbook + tabletop; Sasha -> coordinate rollout to dedicated and staging, add to dashboard. Can someone paste the k6 snippet and the cron we want?

priya: k6 quick snippet to start with (we'll expand in repo):

```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  http.post('https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({input: 'x'.repeat(200)}), { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $TOKEN' } });
  sleep(0.5);
}

// Cron schedule for weekly stable run: 0 2 * * 1  # Mondays at 02:00 UTC
```

jamie: For the regression harness, I'll add a promptset named evict-longseq-2026-03 with ~250 cases: mixture of long-context summaries, repeated short queries, and adversarial tokenization edge cases. Will also wire eval metrics: median latency, 95th latency, eviction-rate, and output-drift (BLEU-ish + embedding cosine).

kyle: Chaos drill checklist (first draft):
- [ ] Create isolated staging cluster config with KV eviction thresholds lowered
- [ ] Run synthetic workload (per Priya's k6) for 30m
- [ ] Trigger fallback to medium-quant model variant
- [ ] Measure error rates, latency, and success of fallback
- [ ] Postmortem + action items within 24h

sasha: Perfect. I'm going to create sprint tickets. Please add PR links into this thread when ready. Also, Jamie/Priya/Kyle — can we commit to initial artifacts by 2026-04-02? If any blocker, flag in here by EOD today. :eyes: 

jamie: Ack — aiming for 2026-04-02. I'll open the PR draft today: https://git.redwood/redux/tests/pulls/ID-to-be-updated (will update ID).

priya: Ack. I'll put k6 job in perf-ci (repo: infra/perf/jobs) and add the cron: `0 2 * * 1` for weekly, plus nightly smoke `0 0 * * *`.

kyle: Ack. I'll draft the chaos plan doc and ping SRE for a tabletop run the week after initial artifacts are merged.

ops-bot: Task created: PERF-1123 (k6 load job), TEST-431 (regression promptset), CHAOS-99 (kv-eviction drill). See: https://issues.redwood/browse/PERF-1123

sasha: Thanks @ops-bot. One more ask: can we add an automated eval check into the pre-merge CI that runs a tiny subset (10 cases) of evict-longseq-2026-03 and fails if eviction-rate increases by >5% vs baseline? If so, that will catch regressions early.

jamie: Yep. I'll add the small CI gate and include a baseline artifact for comparison. Will use the eval harness in tests/evals and surface the results in PR checks.

priya: I'll make sure perf-ci exposes kv-miss metrics so the CI gate can read them.

sasha: Great. I'll move these to the sprint board now and follow up on Monday's stand for status. Thanks all. :rocket:

jamie: :thumbsup:

priya: :raised_hands:

kyle: :clap:
